name: Button
hint: Click it. Switch states, theme and mode in the panel.
description: Themed button in primary, secondary, ghost, danger and danger-quiet variants. Presses on a spring; while `loading` it morphs into a circle with a spinner (keeping its place in the layout), and on `success` draws a check before the label returns. It never plays that cycle on its own: you drive it from your async work.
intents: submit button that shows it is saving
usage: Use for every clickable action. One primary per view; secondary and ghost for the rest; danger only for destructive actions, danger-quiet for a destructive action that should not shout (a Remove link in a list, a Cancel subscription in settings). Start with `label` (or children) and `onClick`; set `type="submit"` inside a form. Drive `loading` / `success` from your own async call: while either is on the button will not fire `onClick` or submit again, so a double click cannot run the action twice. `demo` (old name `simulate`) fakes a working-then-done cycle on click for the gallery; it is off by default, leave it off in real UI. One shape per surface, not a mix: to round every button, set `buttonShape="pill"` on `<Theme>`, which also reaches the buttons that Modal, Card, CTA Band and the other components draw. `shape="pill"` rounds this one button whatever the Theme says; the default, `"rounded"`, follows the Theme (its corner size unless `buttonShape` is set).

keyboard.does: Presses the button and calls onClick.
keyboard.when: not loading, showing success or disabled

keyboard.does: Does nothing: the press is dropped, so the action cannot run twice.

screenReader: A native button named by `label` or its text (pass `aria-label` when children are not plain text). While loading it is aria-busy and keeps its label as its name, and a polite live region says "<label>: working", then "<label>: done" on success. Disabled is the native disabled state, so it leaves the Tab order.

dataProps.description: The button text. Also its accessible name while it shows the spinner or the check.
Content instead of `label`, when you need markup. Wins over `label`; pass `aria-label` if it is not plain text.
(event) => void. Called on click unless the button is loading, showing success or disabled. Two clicks in the same tick call it once.
Optional leading icon, rendered before the label.
Native button type. Use "submit" inside a <form>; while loading or success a submit button does not submit again.
You own it: set it when your async work starts and clear it when it ends. Shows the spinner and blocks clicks.
Set it briefly after the work succeeds to draw the check; clicks are blocked while it shows.
Native disabled: not focusable, not clickable, dimmed.
Emphasis. danger-quiet is an outlined danger for destructive actions that should not be the loudest thing on screen.
Height of the button: 34px, 42px or 52px. On a phone or a touch screen every size is at least 44px tall.
Fill the width of the container. Use it for the one action of a form or a phone bar.
Any other button attribute (name, value, form, aria-label, aria-describedby, data-*, tabIndex) goes to the <button>. className and style are merged with the button's own.
Forwarded to the <button>, so a Button can be a Modal `trigger`, a popover anchor, or be focused after an error.
